encounters.cc: Irritability, decreased appetite, and two days of intermittent fever with ear pain

lines: Irritability, decreased appetite, and two days of intermittent fever with ear pain
A 5-year-old male with asthma and steroid-dependent minimal change disease, hospitalized in January 2020 for nephrotic syndrome, presents with ear pain.
His mother reports that he has been pulling on his right ear, has had difficulty sleeping, and cried throughout the night.
He attends daycare and had a runny nose and nasal congestion one week ago that seemed to improve before the ear pain began.
Active Problem List:
- Minimal change disease (diagnosed 2020-01-15)
- Asthma
- Relapsing minimal change disease (steroid-dependent nephrotic syndrome)
He has no chronic illnesses and has received routine childhood immunizations.
Home Medications:
- Fluticasone propionate HFA inhaler 44 mcg per inhalation, 2 puffs inhaled twice daily
No known drug allergies
- Maternal history of asthma and eczema
- Paternal history of allergic rhinitis
- No family history of kidney disease or autoimmune disorders
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: Never. Occupation: Kindergarten student.
He does not complain of sore throat, vomiting, or abdominal pain.
On examination, his temperature is 38.4 °C (101.1 °F), pulse is 110/min, and respirations are 22/min.
He appears uncomfortable but is alert and cooperative.
Oropharynx is mildly erythematous without exudates, lungs are clear, and no skin rash is seen.
Otoscopic evaluation of the right ear reveals a bulging, erythematous tympanic membrane with decreased mobility when insufflated.

His asthma had been well-controlled on inhaled corticosteroids until a recent upper respiratory tract infection.

He is brought to the rheumatology clinic by his mother due to a rash and joint pain that started 2 days ago.
The mother reports that the child had an upper respiratory tract infection last week, which resolved without treatment.
The boy complains of pain in his knees and ankles, which worsens with movement.

lines: Rash on his legs and abdominal pain for the past two days
The patient is an 11-year-old male with steroid-dependent minimal change disease and prior Henoch-Schönlein purpura who returns with rash and abdominal pain.
His parents state that he has been less playful and complained of "tummy aches" after meals, sometimes curling up in discomfort.
They note swelling in his knees and ankles, and he walks with a limp.
He had a mild cough and runny nose about a week ago that resolved spontaneously, and the parents deny any fever, bleeding, or recent medication use.

encounters.cc: Swelling around eyes and difficulty breathing

lines: Swelling around eyes and difficulty breathing

The patient is a 13-year-old male with steroid-dependent minimal change disease and asthma who returns with recurrent edema and respiratory symptoms, having experienced multiple prior nephrotic syndrome relapses and previous pulmonary complications.
He reports that the swelling started two days ago.
The mother reports that his face looks puffier in the morning and that his legs have started to appear swollen as well.
Over the past day, he has also developed a dry cough and mild shortness of breath when walking around the house.
His appetite has been poor, but he has not had fever, vomiting, or diarrhea.
He had a mild sore throat a few weeks ago that resolved on its own.
